title: Evaluating RAG: Retrieval, Grounding and Failures
summary: A RAG answer can be wrong because retrieval missed the evidence, because the wrong chunk ranked first, because the model ignored the context, or because the data was stale. This lesson defines the metrics for each stage, a failure taxonomy for diagnosis, and how to build and trust an evaluation set.
objectives: Compute context precision, context recall and average precision for a retrieved list
Compute faithfulness, answer relevance and citation precision/recall from claim-level judgements
Classify RAG failures into missed retrieval, wrong chunk, ignored context, stale data and other causes, and prioritise fixes from a failure tally
Size an evaluation set and compute a confidence interval for a measured accuracy
Describe what to monitor in production: freshness, not-found rate, citation use, latency and cost
prerequisites: You should know the retrieval metrics from [Hybrid Search and Reranking](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/hybrid-and-reranking), the accuracy equation from [How RAG Works](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/rag-architecture), and the idea of an LLM judge ([Using a Model as a Judge](/learn/evaluation/llm-as-judge)).
